title: Transit Orchestrator: latency- and capacity-aware multi-region request gate
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a Transit Orchestrator service that centralizes multi-region request routing decisions using: latency budgets, geo-pinning heuristics, and live capacity hints. The goal is a conservative, observable gate that prevents cross-region amplification during overloads and enforces graceful degradation by combining circuit-breaker signals with probabilistic shedding. This ticket covers design, canary implementation, telemetry and initial rollout for a single product route (text-generation/v1).
background: We have recurring incidents where aggressive hedging and blanket regional failover cause cascading resource exhaustion in secondary regions. Current per-region steering is distributed and opaque; there is inconsistent behavior when capacity is constrained (e.g., broad hedges that spike remote GPU pools). Our SLOs include 99th percentile p95 token latency and regional availability thresholds. We need a middle layer that enforces global policies while respecting regional capacity and locality preferences.
goals: Enforce per-request routing decision that balances latency budget and capacity hints
Add geo-pinning with soft-fallbacks to avoid unhealthy mass failovers
Introduce a circuit-breaker state machine to quarantine problematic regions and routes
Provide clear telemetry surfaces for SLO compliance and cost impact
Roll out to text-generation/v1 route behind a canary flag with safe defaults
success_metrics: Reduce cross-region failover-induced CPU/GPU burst incidents by >= 70% within first month
No more than 1.5x increase in 95th percentile latency for canary traffic vs baseline
Maintain regional availability >= 99.9% for pinned regions during steady state
Shedding events should recover to <0.1% of global requests under normal load
telemetry_queries: Capacity hint health: custom.ingress.capacity_hints - boolean per region per model
Circuit state churn: traces.transit_orch.circuit_events - count of OPEN/CLOSED/QUARANTINE
Cross-region traffic delta: metric:requests.per_region.delta(5m) - detect sudden hedges
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal dev): run transit-orch behind flag for 5% of internal dev traffic to text-generation/v1 for 72h
Phase B (canary): enable for 1% of customer production traffic with dashboard + alerting; run for 1 week
Phase C (regional ramp): target 10% traffic in US regions and 1% in EU/APAC to validate geo pin logic
Phase D (full): enable by default with opt-out per-customer; monitor cost and SLOs for 2 weeks
acceptance_criteria: Transit Orchestrator returns a routing decision within 4ms P95 for proxy-invoked requests
Decision payload includes: chosen_region, candidate_list (with score), circuit_state, shed_probability
Circuit-breaker transitions are logged and surfaced in Console with links to incident traces
Automated tests for: latency budget enforcement, pinned region preference, and probabilistic shedding under overload
On canary, no regression detected in end-to-end latency SLO above 1.5x baseline at P95
risks: Added centralization increases latency/availability risk if Transit Orchestrator becomes a single point of failure
Incorrect capacity hints could bias routing and starve healthy regions if heuristics are wrong
Overly aggressive shedding might degrade customer experience before fallbacks kick in
Complexity of state machine could produce oscillations (flip-flopping circuits) under near-threshold conditions
mitigations: Deploy transit-orch as a highly-available service with regional replicas and local cache of decisions
Fallback to local routing logic when transit-orch is unreachable (stateless, best-effort hedging)
Conservative default thresholds and slow ramp for shedding probabilities; require two-window confirmation for circuit open
Add hysteresis timers and rate-limit circuit state changes to avoid oscillation
decisions: Use a hybrid scoring function: score = latency_headroom_weight * latency_score + capacity_weight * capacity_score + geo_preference_weight * locality_score
Circuit-breaker states: CLOSED, SOFT_OPEN (probabilistic shedding), HARD_OPEN (rejects), QUARANTINE (regional excluded for X minutes)
Capacity hints modeled as three levels: GREEN/AMBER/RED from regional autoscaler + pool utilization signals
Pinning uses tokens: requests carry pin_hint; if model pinned and region healthy prefer pinned region; else apply soft-fallbacks
implementation_notes: Transit-orch exposes a lightweight gRPC API consumed by edge proxies; response size < 512 bytes
Decisions cached per-route+model for 200ms at proxies to reduce request amplification; cache invalidation via push when circuit state changes
Shedding implemented as probabilistic reject with client-visible 429 and explicit 'x-redwood-shed' header for observability
Integrate with Console: add per-route circuit timeline and a per-region capacity heatmap
dependencies: ENG-412002 (capacity-hints pipeline) - needs stable capacity signals
ENG-405987 (edge proxy integration) - header contract and caching semantics
PM-204 (product signoff on default shedding thresholds)
notes: We intentionally avoid full request redirection at the proxy layer for the first canary; proxies will consult transit-orch and continue local hedging when transit-orch is unavailable
Do not enable automatic model variant fallback in Phase A; keep decision explicit to observe behavior
Consider later addition: tokenized credit system so low-priority tenants are shed first during capacity pressure
